solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Miser upset about landlord's political belief in the US

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters are placed on either side of the next piece
upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: a landlord, in British usage, is a publican who runs a pub; the 's is just possessive glue

explanation.surface: A grumpy miser objects to a landlord's politics, American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MISER into RE...ISM, which goes 'about' PUBLICAN. In Britain the landlord of a pub is the publican.
explanation.definitionFit: Republicanism is the creed of the Republican Party, one of the two main American parties.

clue.text: Tough case of decay limiting public transport

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on either side, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: rot is a case of decay
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A hard instance of rot is curbing the bus service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' tempts you to take outer letters of decay; it is just an instance of decay, ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and sturdy, able to withstand hard treatment.

clue.text: Peel 'n' a pip has the makings of a fruit

indicators.note: the makings are raw materials, so these letters are reworked to build the answer

explanation.surface: Fruit peel and a pip are the ingredients for a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Element oxygen many initially discovered in sea water

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside, so the two letters sit within the sea water

parts.note: brine is salt water, such as the sea

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A chemist finds oxygen and much else in sea water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' applies to both oxygen and many, not just the word beside it; 'discovered in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromine is a chemical element, a red-brown liquid halogen extracted from seawater.

clue.text: Absolutely certain company is into table tennis, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Oddly, a firm has taken up ping-pong.
explanation.definitionFit: Incontestable means beyond dispute, so something incontestable is certain.

clue.text: Six into articles about birds

indicators.note: into places the Roman numeral inside the two articles

parts.note: a and an are both indefinite articles
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six pieces were written on the subject of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like magazine pieces; it is grammar's A and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian is the adjective for birds, as in avian flu, a disease of birds.

clue.text: Annoy when spilling kir

indicators.note: spilling a drink sends it everywhere, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Knocking over a cocktail is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: To irk is to irritate or bother someone.

clue.text: Got together outside popular university dance

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the meeting word wraps around the others

parts.note: met means got together
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Students met up outside a popular university dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The minuet is a stately seventeenth-century ballroom dance in triple time.

clue.text: Jack's entering bar with old sort of guitar

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece is placed inside the others

parts.note: to bar is to ban
J is the card abbreviation for jack; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack walks into a pub with an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but here it is the verb meaning ban.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a stringed instrument plucked like a guitar, with a drum-like round body.

clue.text: Cowardly chap is after elegance and style

indicators.note: is after means the man's name comes behind the other piece in the answer

parts.note: chic means elegance and stylishness
Ken is a typical man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A timid man pursues a sophisticated, stylish partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' looks like romantic pursuit, but it only says the name follows CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is informal for timid or lacking courage, as in daring someone not to be chicken.

clue.text: Rubbish in Jerusalem rail terminus?

indicators.note: in places the piece for rubbish inside the name for Jerusalem

parts.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, a poetic name for Jerusalem
tat is cheap, tasteless rubbish

explanation.surface: Litter is piling up at a railway terminal in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a station need not be a terminus. SION is the less common spelling of Zion.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the end stop of a railway line, which is one kind of station.

clue.text: Some panic here in specialised part of the market

definitions.text: in specialised part of the market

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Traders are in a panic in a small, specialised market sector.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche market is a small specialised segment of trade serving particular buyers.

clue.text: Hole in skin interrupting pink of the body

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the hole sits inside the colour

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A spot on rosy skin disturbs the body's complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means physical or bodily, relating to the flesh rather than the spirit.

clue.text: Pressure concerning young claimant to the throne

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means concerning or about
tender can mean young, as in 'of tender years'

explanation.surface: A youthful rival claimant comes under pressure over the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender asserts a right to a crown held by someone else, like the Old Pretender.

clue.text: Period without a drink is difficult after start of drinking time

indicators.note: after says the difficult piece follows the first letter in the answer
start of takes just the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: rough means hard or difficult

explanation.surface: Going dry is hard just after opening time at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long spell with no rain, cryptically a period lacking drink.

clue.text: Some fissure turned up as a source of life

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
Some says a run of letters is taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crack has opened, revealing where life comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' is part of the text to search; 'up' alone signals the backwards reading of SURETU.
explanation.definitionFit: The uterus, or womb, is where a foetus develops before birth.

clue.text: Good first appearance needed for the upper crust

parts.note: an entry is a first appearance, as an actor's entry on stage

explanation.surface: A debut must be impressive among high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born social class just below the nobility, the upper crust.

clue.text: Tons lacking power to make changes

parts.note: weak means lacking power or strength

explanation.surface: Heavy loads with no power behind them need adjusting.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to adjust slightly, making small alterations to improve something.

clue.text: Fabric sounding like something driver should carry

indicators.note: sounding like says the answer is said the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: a driver should carry a car key

explanation.surface: A fabric that sounds like a motorist's essential.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, with no r sounded, car key and khaki sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a sturdy dull-brown cloth used for military uniforms.

clue.text: A couple of people owe most, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pair of people are deeply in debt, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair, two people doing something together.

clue.text: Right pub in centre offering this item in crumble?

indicators.note: in places the word for a pub inside the word for a centre

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A proper town-centre pub serves this pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumble is a British baked pudding of stewed fruit under a crumbly topping; rhubarb is a classic filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb stalks are cooked like fruit and are a traditional filling for a baked crumble dessert.

clue.text: Royal Navy is after universal vessel

indicators.note: is after means the navy's letters come behind the other piece

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: The navy is chasing a vessel that goes anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a container. U is the British film rating suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, so a vessel in the sense of a receptacle.

clue.text: Leading pair abandoning the most doubtful visitor

indicators.note: the first two letters leave the word, so its opening pair is dropped

parts.note: vaguest means the most uncertain or doubtful

explanation.surface: The two front-runners walk away from the dodgiest caller.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone visiting a home or staying at a hotel.

clue.text: Enraptured current chaps score romantically

parts.note: sent is old slang for thrilled or enraptured
I is the physics symbol for electric current
men are chaps
a tally is a score or count

explanation.surface: Thrilled young men now score love songs with feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimentally means with tender, nostalgic feeling, much as romantically does.
